description:
NovaGlitch is a team from Pakistan taking part in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 through the Islamabad local event. We love space, and we joined to work with real NASA data and help solve a space problem.

We chose "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" and built the Jezero Traverse Map, an interactive web map of Jezero Crater that uses machine learning and route planning to find safe walking routes for astronauts on Mars.
summary: The Jezero Traverse Map is an interactive web map that helps a suited astronaut plan a safe walk across the delta area of Jezero Crater on Mars. It layers four kinds of real NASA and USGS data: topography, optical images, thermal images and geology. Slope and hillshade are calculated from a 20 m elevation model, and a k-means machine learning step sorts the ground into four terrain types. An A* route planner then finds a path that never crosses a slope over 20 degrees. The safe route is 5.62 km and about 140 minutes with a steepest step of 10 degrees, while a straight line is 5.53 km, about 155 minutes and 19.6 degrees. The map runs in any browser with no install.
details:
THE PROBLEM

Astronauts walking on Mars cannot simply go in a straight line. Steep slopes and rough ground slow them down, tire them and can be dangerous in a suit. A photo alone does not show how steep or rough the ground is. Users are crews planning surface walks, mission planners, and students or the public who want to understand how Mars exploration is planned.

WHAT WE BUILT

An interactive map of a 14 by 15 km area of Jezero Crater with layers you can switch on and off: elevation, hillshade, slope, terrain classes, optical (CTX), thermal day and night (THEMIS) and 11 USGS geologic units. It includes hover read-outs and a HUD view where you can drag a slider along the planned route.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Slope and hillshade are calculated from the elevation model.

2. K-means (machine learning) groups the ground into 4 terrain types using slope and roughness.

3. An A* planner finds the cheapest path. Slopes over 20 degrees are not allowed, rougher ground costs more, and level-ground speed is 2.7 km/h.

4. The route is compared with a straight line and re-run with different terrain costs. It stays the same (100% within 200 m).

RESULT

Safe route: 5.62 km, about 140 min, steepest step 10.0 degrees. Straight line: 5.53 km, about 155 min, 19.6 degrees.

LIMITS AND ASSUMPTIONS

Terrain cost factors are assumptions. The 20 degree limit comes from secondary Artemis guidance and 2.7 km/h from Apollo-based walking analysis. Mars gravity (0.38 g) is not modelled, and 20 m pixels hide boulders and loose sand.

FUTURE WORK

An offline app that runs on suit or habitat computers (Mars has no internet and signals take minutes), with a small on-device AI assistant that explains route choices.

USE OF AI

Claude (Anthropic) helped plan the project and write and debug the code. All layers are computed from the cited datasets, with no AI-generated imagery. The narration voice in the demo video is AI-generated (ElevenLabs). Disclosed in the README, code headers, the map page and the slides.
